questions.question: Works locally but breaks in prod, teammates get different installs, a merge conflict blocks the PR — the debugging playbook?
questions.title: Tooling Scenarios
questions.direct_answer: The four classic tooling scenarios: (1) WORKS LOCIALLY, FAILS DEPLOYED — the divergence is the ENVIRONMENT: reproduce with a production build locally first (npm run build && start), then diff env vars (the #1 cause — missing/renamed vars in CI), Node versions, and case-sensitivity (macOS is case-INSENSITIVE, Linux servers are not — './Button' vs './button' works locally, 404s in prod). (2) DIFFERENT INSTALLS ACROSS TEAMMATES — the lockfile isn't committed or CI runs npm install instead of npm ci: install honors the lockfile but may RESOLVE if ranges drift; ci installs EXACTLY the lockfile, failing if out of sync — commit the lockfile, use npm ci in CI. (3) MERGE CONFLICT BEFORE A PR — rebase onto the target branch, resolve per-hunk by INTENT (not just making text agree), run tests, and when a conflict repeats a semantic change, prefer the version that matches the new architecture. (4) SLOW BUNDLE — analyze with a bundle visualizer: the usual suspects are a dependency imported at top level when only one function is used, barrel files re-exporting everything, and duplicated versions from transitive deps.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The playbook per scenario, verified:

```bash
# 1. WORKS LOCALLY, FAILS IN PROD �� reproduce FIRST
npm run build && npm run start     # most 'prod-only' bugs reproduce here
# then diff the environment:
env | grep -i next                # missing vars? renamed? NEXT_PUBLIC_ inlined?
node --version                    # version parity with the server
# case-sensitivity: fine on macOS, 404 on Linux
#   grep -rn "from '\./Button'" src/    — check the FILE is Button.tsx not button.tsx

# 2. DIFFERENT INSTALLS — lockfile discipline
git ls-files | grep lock          # is the lockfile committed?
npm ci                            # EXACTLY the lockfile — fails if out of sync
npm install                       # may RESOLVE newer versions within ranges
# team rule: commit the lockfile, CI runs ci, updates go through renovate/dependabot PRs

# 3. MERGE CONFLICT BEFORE THE PR
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
# per hunk: read BOTH sides' intent, not just the markers
#   ours: the feature change   theirs: the newer main change
#   resolve to the version that satisfies BOTH intents
npm test && npm run build         # green before pushing

# 4. SLOW BUNDLE — measure, then cut
npx next build --profile          # or @next/bundle-analyzer
# usual suspects: barrel imports, top-level heavy deps, transitive duplicates
import { debounce } from 'lodash-es'        // fine (tree-shakeable)
import _ from 'lodash'                      // 70KB+ when you wanted one fn
const Chart = () => import('react-chartjs-2') // lazy: route-level split
```

The reasoning per scenario (the interview structure):
1. The local/prod divergence has four roots in order of likelihood: env vars, case-sensitivity, Node version, host config. The discipline: NEVER debug on the live host when a local production build can reproduce — env is testable, case-sensitivity greppable, versions comparable.
2. Different installs mean the lockfile ISN'T the source of truth: either it isn't committed, or something runs install and re-resolves. ci's fail-on-mismatch is the guarantee — a red CI saying 'lockfile out of sync' is the system working.
3. Conflicts resolve by INTENT: the markers show WHERE text disagrees; the fix is understanding WHAT each side was trying to do. 'Accept theirs' is right when the base version died; wrong when it silently reverts your fix. Tests are the arbiter.
4. Bundle weight is measured, never guessed: the analyzer shows the actual chunks. Barrels (index.ts re-exporting everything) defeat tree-shaking for transitive deps; dynamic imports split code by route; npm ls dup finds version duplication to dedupe.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SYM{symptom} -->|local ok prod broken| L1[reproduce: build + start locally]
    L1 --> L2[env vars — the #1 cause]
    L1 --> L3[case sensitivity: macOS vs Linux]
    L1 --> L4[Node version parity]
    SYM -->|teammates differ| I1[lockfile not the truth]
    I1 --> F1['commit lockfile + npm ci in CI — fail on drift']
    SYM -->|conflict blocks PR| M1[rebase onto target]
    M1 --> F2[resolve per hunk by intent + tests green]
    SYM -->|bundle slow| B1[measure with an analyzer]
    B1 --> F3[cut: direct imports over barrels, lazy route code, dedupe]
    LOCAL[debug on a local prod build] -.never.-> HOST[the live host]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The case-sensitivity class (the most embarrassing prod-only bug family): macOS/Windows filesystems match './utils/Helpers' to helpers.ts; Linux does not — a deploy that builds locally and 404s on a module is almost always an import-case mismatch. The systematic fix: a lint rule (eslint-plugin-import's case-sensitive check) or a CI job running on Linux from day one (the build IS the case-sensitivity test when CI is Linux and dev is macOS). Same family: files differing only in case in git (config core.ignorecase) — two files where one machine sees one.

Lockfile mechanics deeper (why install can drift): install with a lockfile present uses it UNLESS a manifest's range no longer matches anything in it (someone edited package.json without installing) — then it re-resolves just that subtree, silently, and rewrites the lockfile. npm ci treats ANY mismatch as a hard error — which is why it's the CI tool and why 'just run install' on a CI box is a policy violation in a disciplined team. The ecosystem extension: pnpm/yarn have the same install-vs-frozen modes (frozen-lockfile in CI) — the concept is universal even when the command differs.

The bundle-cutting toolbox in full (scenario 4's professional close): (a) direct imports from files, not barrels (import x from 'lib/x' not 'lib') — or configure path aliases that point INTO the module; (b) route-level code splitting: next/dynamic per heavy region (charts, editors, admin tables) — load what the user sees first, defer the rest; (c) dedupe: npm ls <dep> shows where multiple versions enter; resolutions/overrides force one — smaller tree, better caching; (d) measure the WATERFALL too: the initial JS isn't the only cost — chunk loading order and blocking scripts matter; (e) server components (Next) move heavy data-shaping OFF the client entirely — the cheapest client bundle is the one that never ships. The one-liner: 'analyze before cutting, cut by route, and suspect the barrel file first.'
